shortNodes.text: Sit down and let the chair take your weight.
Keep the eyes open, with a soft gaze.
Point at something in front of you — a wall, a cup, a window.
Now turn the finger around, and point at the place where others would see your face.
Looking now, not from memory — is there a face here, or open space?
Thoughts will arrive. Treat them as trains. You can watch them pass without boarding.
If you already got on one, notice that. Step back onto the platform.
Rest as the space this is all happening in.
When you stand, stand as the same space.

longNodes.text: Find a seat you can stay in without fussing.
Let the chair take your weight. You do not have to hold yourself up.
Keep the eyes open. A soft gaze is enough — not staring, not shut.
Take in whatever is in front of you — the color, the light, the simple fact of seeing.
Now point at something out there. A wall, a cup, a window.
Notice that it is a thing, with color and shape, at a distance.
Turn the finger around, and point at the place where others would see your face.
On present evidence — looking now, not from memory — is there a color here? A shape? A face?
What is actually given on this side of the finger?
If you find space instead of a face, you are not missing something. You are seeing what is here.
Thoughts will arrive. Treat them as trains. You can read the destination without getting on.
If you already boarded, that boarding is just another train, visible from the platform.
You are not a passenger. You are the space the trains pass through.
A memory of the past is an image appearing now. A plan for the future is a picture appearing now.
I will be quiet for a while. Stay with this looking. If you get lost, point in again.
Let the finger rest. The looking can stay without the gesture.
Carry this into the next ordinary thing.

shortNodes.text: Sit so you can forget the sitting. Eyes open.
Point out at a thing. See it clearly — color, shape, distance.
Now point back at where others see your face.
What is here, on this side of the finger?
The world is there. Space is here. Both at once.
Let a thought pass through that space. Do not follow it.
Check again. Still no face?
Rest as that.

longNodes.text: Sit so you can forget the sitting.
Eyes stay open. Take in the room without naming it well.
Point at a wall, or a cup, or a window. A thing, out there.
Now point at your chest. Also a thing, with a location.
Now point at the place others see your face.
Single question: looking at what is given, is there a face here?
Color? Shape? A pair of eyes? Or space, for the whole world to appear in?
Keep one finger pointing in, and one pointing out.
The world is there. No face here. Both at once. This is two-way looking.
You can rest the hands. The looking does not need the gesture.
Sounds appear in this same space. Thoughts appear in this same space.
Nothing to improve, and no one behind the view who needs to wake up.
I will be quiet. If you drift, point in again. What is here?
Stand as the same no-face the room is appearing in.

shortNodes.text: Sit easy. Eyes can close, or stay softly open.
Is it possible to imagine the space between your eyes?
The space between your ears.
The space inside the mouth, and the throat.
Now the space around the body — behind you, above you, below the seat.
See if inside and outside can be one continuous space.
Rest in that. Diffuse is enough.

longNodes.text: Sit easy. You can close the eyes, or leave them soft.
Is it possible to imagine the space between your eyes?
Can you imagine the space between your ears?
The space inside your throat. Not the throat. The space.
Can you imagine space between the fingers — all of them at once?
Hands filled with space. Arms filled with space.
The whole body filled with space, as if the body were a volume, not a surface.
Now include the space around the body. Behind you. Above. Below the seat.
See if inside and outside can be one continuous space.
Sounds happening in that space. Thoughts too. You do not have to hold it tight.
Diffuse attention is enough. Wide, not sharp.
I will be quiet. Stay with space, not with objects.
Gently come back. The room is still here.

shortNodes.text: Sit or lie down. Close the mouth. Breathe through the nose.
Let the breath be light. This is not a performance.
A little slower, only if that is easy.
If the mind runs, let it. Keep the nose breathing.
Stay with the next breath only.
That is the whole practice.

longNodes.text: Sit or lie down. Mouth closed. Breathe through the nose.
Let the breath be light, and quiet. Not a performance.
A little slower, if that is easy. No strain.
Feel the air at the nostrils. In. Out.
If you can, let the belly move a little more than the chest.
If the mind runs, let it. You are not failing. Keep the nose breathing.
No need to empty anything. The breath is already happening.
Light. Slow. Low in the body.
I will be quiet. Stay with the next breath only.
That is the whole practice. Nothing else to get right.

shortNodes.text: Sit. Eyes open. Leave the view as it is.
There is already knowing here. You do not have to make it.
A thought appears. Let it be a thought. Do not follow, do not fight.
Rest as the knowing in which the thought appeared.
If you get involved, notice that. That noticing is the same knowing.
Leave it. Already awake is not a future state.

longNodes.text: Sit. Eyes open. Leave the view as it is.
You do not need a special state. Knowing is already happening.
Look: who is looking? Do not answer with a story. Look.
Whatever appears — sound, thought, the room — appears in this knowing.
You do not have to hold the knowing. It holds the appearances.
A thought about practice is just another appearance. Let it go by.
No need to improve this moment, or to become someone who is meditating well.
If you get lost, that getting lost is known. Rest there.
I will be quiet. Leave everything as it is.
This was not a technique to keep. It is what is always the case.

shortNodes.text: Sit upright, at ease. Eyes open or barely so.
Turn attention around, as if mind were looking at mind.
What does mind look like, when you look directly?
If you find no thing there, do not fill the gap. Leave it.
Thoughts can move. Mind remains unstained, like space.
Rest. Do not meddle.

longNodes.text: Sit upright, at ease. Eyes open, or barely open.
For a moment, let attention rest on the breath. Then let even that go.
Turn the looking around. Let mind look at mind.
What do you find? A shape? A color? A watcher sitting behind the eyes?
If you find no object there, that is not a failure. That is the look.
Thoughts may still arise. Let them arise and dissolve, like writing on water.
You do not have to stop them. You do not have to follow them.
Leave mind as it is. Fresh. Uncontrived. Already free.
I will be quiet. If you start managing the mind, drop the managing.
Nothing to take with you. The looking is already yours.

shortNodes.text: Sit upright. Not stiff. Awake.
Eyes lowered. Soft gaze on the floor ahead.
This is the practice. Nothing extra.
A thought arrives. Open the hand of thought. Let it go.
Return is not a failure. Return is the practice.
Just sit.

longNodes.text: Sit upright. Not stiff. Awake.
Eyes lowered. Soft gaze on the floor a few feet ahead.
Hands at rest. Jaw unclenched. This is enough.
You are not here to improve this moment.
A thought arrives. Open the hand of thought.
Return is not a failure. Return is the practice.
Sounds, pressure, breath — they belong to the same sitting.
Do not add a story about how well this is going.
I will be quiet. Just sit.
When the time ends, stand without leaving.

shortNodes.text: Sit. Let the body be quiet.
A thought is here. Ask, gently: who is this appearing to?
Do not answer with a name, or a story. Look.
Whatever you find — or fail to find — stay with that.
The one who would finish this practice is another thought.
Rest as what does not come and go.

longNodes.text: Sit. Let the body be quiet. Soft eyes, or closed.
Notice a thought, or a feeling, as it appears.
Ask, gently: who is this appearing to?
Do not answer with a name. Do not answer with a biography. Look.
If a person appears as the answer, that person is another object. Who is it appearing to?
You are not looking for a better thought. You are looking for the one who thinks.
What remains when the answer falls silent?
I will be quiet. Keep the question alive, without chasing it.
There is nothing to conclude. Leave it open.

shortNodes.text: Sit still. Eyes closed if that helps.
Feel the breath at the nostrils, or the belly. That is the home base.
When a thought pulls you, note it — thinking — and return.
When a sound appears, note hearing, and return.
You are not trying to stop anything. You are seeing it change.
Keep returning. That is the practice.

longNodes.text: Sit still. Eyes closed if that helps.
Feel the breath at the nostrils, or at the belly. Let that be home base.
When attention wanders, you will notice. That noticing is mindfulness.
Note it simply. Thinking. Hearing. Pressure. Then return to the breath.
Do not narrate a story about the thought. One word is enough. Then let it go.
Pleasant or unpleasant — same instruction. See it. Let it change.
Nothing here is a problem to solve. Everything here is passing.
I will be quiet. Note, and return.
Open the eyes. The same seeing can walk out of the room.

shortNodes.text: Sit comfortably. Close the eyes.
Rest attention on the breath, wherever it is easiest to feel.
When you wander, come back. No commentary.
The breath does not need to be special. Ordinary breathing is the object.
Stay. Return. Stay.

longNodes.text: Sit comfortably, with a straight back. Close the eyes.
Rest attention on the breath, wherever it is easiest — nostrils, chest, or belly.
Let the breath be natural. You are watching, not driving.
When attention wanders, notice, and place it back. That is the whole skill.
No drama about wandering. A wandering mind is the reason for the practice.
If it helps, feel one whole in-breath, then one whole out-breath.
I will be quiet. Stay with the breath. Return as many times as you need.
Let the attention widen. Then open the eyes.

shortNodes.text: Sit easy. Soften the face.
Bring to mind yourself, as you are right now. Not the improved version.
Quietly: may I be safe. May I be at ease.
If that feels false, do not force it. Offer the wish anyway, like setting a cup down.
Now someone easy to care for. May you be safe. May you be at ease.
Let that be enough.

longNodes.text: Sit easy. Soften the face and the hands.
Bring to mind yourself, as you actually are. Not a better edition.
Say, inwardly, and slowly: may I be safe. May I be at ease. May I not be governed by these trains of thought.
If warmth does not come, that is fine. The words are the practice, not the mood.
Now someone who is easy to care for. See their face. May you be safe. May you be at ease.
A neutral person — someone you pass and do not think about. The same wish.
If you can, include someone difficult, without pretending the history is gone. May you be free from suffering.
Widen once: all of us, in this same predicament. May we be at ease.
I will be quiet. Rest in the wish, or in the simple fact of sitting.
Come back. Keep one phrase if you want it: may I be at ease.

shortNodes.text: Sit. Close the eyes if you like.
Notice who is here. A worried part, a driven part, a tired part. Do not pick a fight.
Ask, inwardly: how old does this part feel? Then wait.
You are not the part. You are the space it is appearing in.
Thank it for trying to help. You can drive from the platform.
Rest as that wider space.

longNodes.text: Sit. Close the eyes if you like.
Notice who showed up. A worried part, a critic, a pusher, a tired one.
Do not merge with it, and do not exile it. See it, as you would see a train.
Ask, inwardly: what are you afraid would happen if you did not do this job?
Wait. Parts speak in images, in tightness, in half-sentences. That counts.
You are not the part. You are the one who can listen. The platform, not the passenger.
If another part jumps in to manage this one, notice that too. Room for both.
Thank them. They have been working. You can take the wheel for now.
I will be quiet. Stay in the space that can hold all of them.
Come back slowly. No need to resolve the story.

shortNodes.text: Sit or stand. Mouth closed. Breathe in through the nose.
On the next out-breath, hum a single easy tone. Not loud. Just a hum.
Again. In through the nose. Hum on the way out. Let the chest and face vibrate.
If a thought comes, let the tone hold you instead of the thought.
Keep humming. I will be quiet while you do.
Stop. Feel the silence after the sound.

longNodes.text: Sit or stand. Shoulders easy. Mouth closed.
Breathe in through the nose. On the out-breath, hum a single easy tone.
Not a performance. A low, ordinary hum, as if warming the voice.
Feel it in the chest, the throat, the face. Let the vibration be the object.
Again. In through the nose. Hum on the way out.
If the mind runs, you are not failing. Come back to the next hum.
You can pause between hums. The silence is part of it.
I will be quiet. Keep an easy rhythm. Stop if you get lightheaded.
Let the last hum fade. Sit in the after-sound.
Open the eyes. The room is still humming, in its way.

shortNodes.text: Sit. Choose one simple sound. Ah, om, or a word you already use.
On the out-breath, say it. Out loud if you can, or under the breath.
Again. Same sound. No melody required.
Let the sound carry the attention. You do not have to think the sound.
Continue. I will be quiet.
Stop. Hear the room.

longNodes.text: Sit. Choose one simple sound. Ah, om, or a mantra you already trust.
This is not theater. One word, repeated, until it holds you.
On the next out-breath, say it. Out loud if the room allows, or quietly.
Again. Same sound. Same pace as the breath.
If you lose the word, pick it up on the next out-breath. That is the practice.
Thoughts will try to board. Let the sound be the platform.
I will be quiet. Keep the sound going, easy and even.
Let the last repetition fade. Sit in what remains.
Open the eyes. You can keep the word in the pocket of the day.

shortNodes.text: Lie down, or sit. Close the eyes if that helps.
Feel the feet. No need to change them. Just the sensation.
Feel the lower legs, the knees, the thighs.
Belly, chest, the small movement of breathing.
Feel the hands, the arms, the shoulders, the face.
The whole body as one field of sensation. Rest there.

longNodes.text: Lie down, or sit supported. Close the eyes if that helps.
Feel the feet. Warmth, pressure, tingling — whatever is actually here.
Move to the lower legs, and the knees. No need to fix anything.
Thighs. Pelvis. The contact with the seat or the floor.
Belly. Chest. Notice the breath moving, without taking it over.
Hands. Arms. Shoulders. Let them be heavy.
Neck. Jaw. The space of the mouth. The eyes in their sockets.
Now the whole body at once, as one field of sensation.
I will be quiet. Stay with the whole, or return to any part that calls.
Wiggle the fingers. Open the eyes. Come back slowly.

shortNodes.text: Stand. Phone away. Eyes open.
Feel the weight in both feet.
Begin to walk, slower than usual. Heel, then sole, then toes.
When the mind leaves, it is not a problem. Come back to the next step.
Keep walking. The step is the sit.
Stop. Feel the standing. Then go on with the day.

longNodes.text: Stand. Put the phone away. Eyes open. This is an outdoor practice if you can.
Feel the weight in both feet before you move.
Begin to walk a little slower than usual. No need to look strange. Just unhurried.
Heel, then sole, then toes. Then the other foot.
The eyes can take in the world. You are not staring at your feet.
When a train of thought boards, notice. Come back to the next step.
Sound, air, light — they belong. They do not need a story.
I will be quiet. Keep walking. If you stop at a corner, that standing is the sit too.
Stop. Feel both feet. Then walk on as the same looking.

shortNodes.text: Stand. Feel the floor.
Imagine a simple boundary around this place — a circle, a room, enough space to be in.
Look to one direction. See what is there. Then turn, and see the next.
Four directions, then back to the center. You are the space in the middle.
Rest as that center. Nothing to banish but distraction.
When you are done, the circle can go. The looking can stay.

longNodes.text: Stand. If you know a banishing ritual, you may use its form. If not, this is enough.
Feel the floor. You are in a place, at a time. That is the altar.
Imagine a quiet boundary around this space. Not to keep the world out. To remember where you are.
Face one direction. Look. What is actually there — wall, tree, sky, furniture.
Turn to the next direction. Look again. Then the next. Then the next.
Four looks. Then return to the center. You are not on the perimeter. You are the space inside it.
If thoughts crowd, they are visitors in the circle. They do not run the place.
I will be quiet. Stand in the middle. Eyes open.
When you are done, let the boundary dissolve. Walk out as the same center.

shortNodes.text: Sit. You do not need to hold on to what happened.
If images or feelings are still here, let them be trains. Watch them pass.
Do not build a religion out of a state. States end.
What is here now, without the story of last night or last year?
Rest as the space those leftovers are moving through.
The ordinary day is the integration.

longNodes.text: Sit. You do not need to recreate anything, or to hold on.
If images, insights, or feelings are still moving, let them be trains.
You can watch them with interest. You do not have to board every one.
A beautiful state is still a state. It will end. That is not a failure.
Do not build a religion, a new identity, or a grand theory out of what visited.
Ask only: what is here now, on present evidence?
Point in, if you want. Space here. World there. Same as always.
I will be quiet. Let the leftovers pass. Stay on the platform.
Drink water. Walk. The ordinary day is the practice now.

shortNodes.text: Sit. Pick one simple object — the breath, a sound, or a spot on the wall.
Rest attention there. When it leaves, you will notice. That noticing is the practice.
Return without a story about how you failed.
The object does not have to be interesting. Ordinary is better.
I will be quiet. Stay, wander, return.
Let the focus soften. The same attention can go wide.

longNodes.text: Sit. Choose one object of attention: the breath at the nostrils, or a visual spot.
Place attention there the way you would rest a hand on a table. No grip.
When attention wanders — and it will — notice the wandering as a train leaving.
Step back onto the platform, which is this object, now.
Do not add a second object. One is enough.
If the object itself becomes a thought about the object, return to the raw feel of it.
I will be quiet. Stay, wander, return. That loop is the sit.
Release the object. Notice that attention can rest without a target.

shortNodes.text: Sit easy. Close the eyes.
Take a word you already use, or the word one. This is not a secret. It is a vehicle.
Think it easily, on the breath or off it. No force. No concentration contest.
If it fades, let it fade. If you remember it, pick it up again. Both are correct.
I will be quiet. Easy repetition. No managing.
Drop the word. Sit in what is already here.

longNodes.text: Sit easy. Close the eyes. Nothing to get right.
Use a sound you already know. If you do not have one, use the word one, silently.
Let it repeat itself, lightly, as if humming inwardly. No strain.
Thoughts will come. That is not a problem. The word is not fighting them.
If you forget the word for a while, you were not failing. Pick it up when you notice.
This is not concentration. It is an easy vehicle, then the space it moves in.
I will be quiet. Repeat without effort.
Let the word go. Rest. Then open the eyes.

shortNodes.text: Sit or lie down. Close the eyes.
Picture a simple room you know, just for a moment. Walls, light, a chair.
Now drop the picture. What remains is the seeing itself, even with eyes closed.
If the image comes back, let it. Then notice the space it appears in.
I will be quiet. Image or no image — same space.
Open the eyes. The room you are in is not a picture.

longNodes.text: Sit or lie down. Close the eyes.
Call up a simple place — a room, a path, a tree. Not a fantasy epic. One scene.
See it long enough to be sure it is an image, happening now.
Now let it go. Do not smash it. Just stop feeding it.
What is here when the picture leaves? Darkness, after-image, space — check.
If another picture arrives, that is another train. You are the platform.
The point is not a better movie. The point is to see that seeing is already happening.
I will be quiet. Stay with the space images appear in.
Open the eyes. Two-way looking: world there, space here.

shortNodes.text: Sit or lie down. You can open your eyes or stop this at any time.
Feel the heaviness of the hands, the feet, the jaw.
Each out-breath, a little heavier, as if the chair were doing the work.
You are not going anywhere. You are still the space these sensations appear in.
I will be quiet. Heavy, and aware.
Wiggle the fingers. The heaviness can go. The awareness does not.

longNodes.text: Sit or lie down. You can open your eyes, move, or end this whenever you want.
This is not medical treatment. It is attention, using heaviness as an anchor.
Feel the hands. Let them be heavy. No need to make it happen.
The feet, the legs, the jaw. Each out-breath, a little more given to gravity.
If a part of you stays alert, that is fine. Alertness is not the enemy of rest.
Thoughts may drift. Treat them as trains. Heavy body, open platform.
You are not disappearing. You are the space a heavy body is appearing in.
I will be quiet. Stay heavy, and here.
Count one, two, three. Wiggle the fingers. Open the eyes if they were closed.

shortNodes.text: Stand, or sit if standing is not available. Eyes open.
Feel both feet. Begin a slow sway, as small as you like.
The movement is the sit. You do not have to freeze to be present.
When a thought boards, keep swaying. Come back to the next shift of weight.
I will be quiet. Slow movement. Eyes open.
Stillness now. Same space, not moving.

longNodes.text: Stand if you can. Eyes open. Phone down.
Feel the weight in both feet. Then begin a slow sway, or a slow stretch.
This is not exercise. It is looking, with the body allowed to move.
Notice the next shift of weight. Heel, toe, hip. Ordinary.
Thoughts will try to make this a workout, or a performance. Let those trains pass.
If you want, raise the arms slowly, then let them fall. Same space throughout.
I will be quiet. Keep moving slowly, or pause when the body wants to.
Stand still. The stillness is not more spiritual than the sway.

shortNodes.text: Sit or lie down. Never do this in water, or while driving. Stop if you feel dizzy.
Mouth or nose — take thirty somewhat stronger breaths. Full in, relaxed out.
After the last exhale, rest with empty lungs, only as long as it is easy.
A full breath in, hold a few seconds, then let it go. Ordinary breathing now.
Feel the body. You are the space this energy is happening in, not the storm.
That is one round. Enough.

longNodes.text: Sit or lie down. Not in water. Not while driving. Stop at the first sign of dizziness.
This is one or two rounds only. You are not chasing a state.
Thirty stronger breaths. In fully, out without force. I will leave space for that.
Now, after an exhale, rest empty, only while it is comfortable. No heroics.
Breathe in fully. Hold a few seconds. Let it go. Normal breathing.
Notice the buzz, if there is one, as a sensation. A train, not a self.
If you want a second round, take it now, same way. Or rest.
Ordinary breath. You are the platform. The chemistry is traffic.
Sit until you feel ordinary again. Then stand slowly.

shortNodes.text: Sit. Soft eyes.
This space you are sitting in is not private. The same awareness holds others too.
Wish, simply: may the one who suffers — including you — be free of the extra story.
Now look: the wisher is also an appearance in the same space.
I will be quiet. Open, and kind, without a project.
Carry both — space, and the wish — into the next conversation.

longNodes.text: Sit. Soft eyes. Nothing to become.
Rest as the space in which this body and these thoughts are appearing.
That space is not a private room. Other lives appear in the same kind of knowing.
Let a simple wish form: may we not be governed by the trains we did not choose.
If that wish turns into a project, or a self-image, see that. Return to space.
Compassion without a manager. Emptiness without coldness.
Point in, if you want. No face here. A world there, full of others.
I will be quiet. Stay open. The wish can sit in the background.
Stand as the same space that includes the next person you meet.

shortNodes.text: Sit. This is a map of attention, not a belief you have to join.
Imagine ten places on a tree, from the ground to a crown of space.
Rest for a moment at the crown — open, unoccupied, like the sky.
Descend to the heart. Warmth, if it is there. If not, space will do.
Return to the crown. Same you, two places, one looking.
Drop the map. The tree was a scaffold. The space remains.

longNodes.text: Sit. Eyes soft. This is pathworking as attention only — no ranks, no current to force.
Picture a simple tree of ten stations, from earth at the base to a crown of open sky.
Begin at the crown. Rest as space. Nothing to hold.
Move attention down to wisdom, then to understanding — two sides, one silence between them.
To the heart. If warmth is here, feel it. If not, do not invent it.
To the foundation, the body, the seat. Gravity. Contact.
Now look both ways: crown and root, sky and seat, in one view.
I will be quiet. You can walk the map, or sit as the space the map is drawn in.
Let the diagram go. Two-way looking is enough: world there, space here.
